To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the data mining lifecycle is best viewed as a continuum, with data mining being a process that starts at data collection and ends with deployment.
data warehousing and data mining are complementary and should be used together.

the data mining lifecycle can be broken down into four stages, that each stage has its own lessons and challenges, and that the lessons and challenges are widely applicable to data-mining projects in domains outside of retail e-commerce.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical application of data mining to the real-world problems faced by e-commerce companies, and we believe that our lessons and challenges will benefit others in their efforts to do so.
the application of data mining and knowledge discovery techniques in retail e-commerce.
the practical issues of data mining, rather than with the technical issues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
data mining using e-commerce weblogs is a very complex problem, but it is a problem that can be solved.
there are still many challenges to be addressed in the data mining of e-commerce data.

the data mining process is not as easy and straight-forward as many would like to believe, and that it is important for data mining projects to be managed as a project, with a project manager and project plan, and with the project team being aware of and addressing the lessons and challenges presented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data warehouse is the key to success, but that it is only the first step.
we have learned that the technical challenges of data mining can often be obviated by a well-designed data collection architecture and data warehouse design.
data mining is not just about algorithms; it is also about data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

data mining in the retail e-commerce space is still in its infancy, and that the data mining community needs to work with business partners to understand and solve the real problems that need to be solved.
data mining in e-commerce can and must be treated as a first-class citizen in the enterprise, with the appropriate resources and support.
the data mining lifecycle is not linear, and that the data mining process should be iterative, with the business and technical goals of the project driving the process.
